note: Sized against the snapshot the release builds. maxBytes carries 64 KiB of headroom because a release compiles its commit hash into two generated files (and into anything that embeds them), so the same tree is a few hundred bytes larger inside a release than in a working checkout; without the headroom the budget trips on its own stamp. Raised once, 2026-09-20, for One More Tune: the quiz's module, stylesheet, deck tooling and its proof photograph entered the public source in this release for the first time (seven files, ~616 KiB). That is the application's own source, which the public tree exists to carry, not build output that belongs outside it — and the raise comes with headroom rather than sitting exactly on the new measurement. Raised again, 2026-09-21, for the ipad1 shared disk: its demo project disk is 512 KiB of content inside apps/desktop/app/content/shared-project-disks.js (+561 KiB measured against the previous snapshot, with the writing-route prompt pass adding 16 KiB and this lane's own source ~10 KiB). Again the application's own content rather than build output, and again the raise carries headroom — the measured tree is 130,849,713 bytes against the new 131,600,000. Raised a third time, 2026-09-22, for the two appearances that landed with their artwork: 422 new paths totalling 5.33 MiB, measured file by file against the previous snapshot — 3.36 MiB is the icon families (Big Sur's 236-file set plus the supplement each older era gained), 1.29 MiB is the eight Theme Lab pixel baselines that gate the specimen board, 0.36 MiB is the official site's Big Sur frames and theme art, and the rest is the source, tests and acceptance records that shipped with them. Every one of them is the application's own artwork or the test fixture that guards it, which is what this tree exists to carry; no build output entered the count. The measured tree is 140,245,216 bytes / 5,361 files / 4,062 assets / 88,969,743 asset bytes, and the new limits carry the same kind of margin the two earlier raises did rather than sitting on the measurement.
